section_summary: This section combines W. K. Lyhan’s reports and requests for funds to penetrate Japanese consular and Foreign Office networks with extensive interdepartmental correspondence about alleged Japanese propaganda in Hawaiʻi’s public and Japanese-language schools. Much of the section consists of repeated sets of California Joint Immigration Committee releases, correspondence routed among the Navy, White House, State Department, and Interior Department, and material opposing Hawaiian statehood. It also includes an Embassy report on the Society for International Cultural Relations, reference lists from proposed educational material on Japan, and a miscellaneous Honolulu newspaper page.

subfiles.title: Miscellaneous Honolulu newspaper page
subfiles.from: Nippu Jiji and other news services
subfiles.about: A newspaper page combines a continuing discussion of China’s currency with Japanese-council news and local Hawaiʻi reports.
subfiles.summary: Honolulu newspaper page: a lead on how U.S. silver policy could destabilize China, plus local items on street lighting, accidents, elections and a profile of Toru Kawamoto.

subfiles.title: Lyhan request for funds to pursue Japanese contacts
subfiles.about: Lyhan asks the Secretary of State to finance travel and undercover work involving Japanese consular contacts in California.
subfiles.summary: Lyhan says his consulate contacts led to invitations to meet Japanese consular officials in San Francisco and Los Angeles; he asks about $400 and further support for four to six months, citing references.

subfiles.title: Lyhan transmittal of photostats and Iizuka conversation
subfiles.about: Lyhan forwards evidence of his Japanese contacts and renews his request for State Department financing.
subfiles.summary: Lyhan sends photostats and an account of Iizuka's introduction to Vice Consul General Yonegaki, saying he is nearing the core of Japan's plans in Hawaii; W. K. Lyhan is his League name.

subfiles.title: Gist of Iizuka’s conversation
subfiles.about: Lyhan records Iizuka’s instructions concerning work with Yonegaki and Japanese plans involving Hawaiʻi.
subfiles.summary: Iizuka reportedly tells Lyhan to deal frankly with Yonegaki, promises larger projects, dismisses military ideas of Japanese farming on Hawaii Island, and urges protecting Nakamura's identity.

subfiles.title: Hull request for investigation of Japanese educational propaganda
subfiles.about: Hull asks the Interior Department to investigate whether Japanese-sponsored materials were intended for Hawaiʻi’s public schools.
subfiles.summary: Hull forwards correspondence received through the Navy from V. S. McClatchy and identifies the organization involved as the semi-official Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai. He asks the Bureau of Education to investigate discreetly and notes Helen Gay Pratt’s reported participation in a New York project involving Japanese professors and American school materials.

subfiles.title: Roosevelt transmittal to Under Secretary Phillips
subfiles.about: Roosevelt sends the State Department correspondence about propaganda in Hawaiʻi.
subfiles.summary: Roosevelt sends Under Secretary Phillips correspondence on alleged propaganda in Hawaii that may interest State.

subfiles.title: White House memorandum returning McClatchy correspondence
subfiles.about: McIntyre returns the McClatchy material and relays the President’s instruction that it be shown to State.
subfiles.summary: White House returns McClatchy's correspondence to Roosevelt; McIntyre says he suggested showing it to State.

subfiles.title: Navy memorandum forwarding Japanese-propaganda material
subfiles.about: The Navy forwards McClatchy’s allegations about Japanese propaganda in Hawaiʻi to the White House.
subfiles.summary: Navy memorandum forwarding a California Joint Immigration Committee letter on Japanese propaganda in American schools, which Roosevelt calls of pertinent interest.

subfiles.title: McClatchy letter concerning Japanese material in Hawaiʻi schools
subfiles.about: McClatchy reports allegations that Japanese-directed textbooks and national-defense material were intended for schools in Hawaiʻi.
subfiles.summary: McClatchy cites a Hawaiian legislative petition, news reports that it was pigeonholed, and a Senate Education Committee letter. He encloses California Joint Immigration Committee releases and a Native Sons resolution, offering additional documentation if requested.

subfiles.title: Release 407: Japanese Propaganda in American Public Schools
subfiles.about: The release alleges a Japanese government plan to distribute Japan-oriented educational material in American and Hawaiian schools.
subfiles.summary: It reproduces claims from a Sino-Korean Peoples League protest concerning a Tokyo conference, Prince Fushimi, Setsuechi Aoki, and Okada. The release argues that textbooks and national-defense material would undermine the Americanization of citizens of Japanese ancestry and notes financial support for Japanese cultural-relations work.

subfiles.title: Release 408: Japan’s Psychology and American Interests
subfiles.about: The release connects Japanese imperial ideology with the proposed introduction of Japanese-prepared textbooks into American schools.
subfiles.summary: It portrays Japan as expansionist, citing Matsuoka, Ichimura, Pacific naval policy, and the proposed Nicaragua Canal. It then presents the textbook project and the Sino-Korean Peoples League’s Hawaiʻi protest as further expressions of Japanese propaganda.

subfiles.title: Release 409: High School Students in U.S. to Be Given Books with Correct Information on Japan
subfiles.about: The release reproduces a Japan Times report on plans for Japanese-American committees to compile textbooks about Japan.
subfiles.summary: The proposed books would cover Japanese government, economic and social conditions, and art for American high-school students. A draft was to be shown to Lasker of the Institute of Pacific Relations before joint final compilation.

subfiles.title: Release 410: Japan Proposes to Instruct Our Public School Students
subfiles.about: The release summarizes the Japanese textbook project and the protest lodged against its use in Hawaiʻi.
subfiles.summary: It links the Society for International Cultural Relations to Japanese government funding and major commercial interests and recalls Japanese lobbying at the Institute of Pacific Relations. Quoting Aoki and Okada, it warns that the project included both public-school texts and national-defense material for Japanese-language schools.

subfiles.title: Release 420-A: Will Hawaii Suppress Investigation of Japanese Propaganda in Public Schools
subfiles.about: The release alleges suppression of Lyhan’s petition for an investigation into Japanese propaganda in Hawaiʻi schools.
subfiles.summary: It says Lyhan faced pressure to withdraw his petition and threats of deportation, while he insisted that his charges were documented. The release attributes the textbook’s preparation to Okada, Bruno Lasker, Masamichi Rōyama, and Helen Gay Pratt and warns of further Japanization of young Japanese Americans.

subfiles.title: Hawaiian Senate Education Committee response to Lyhan
subfiles.about: The Senate Education Committee reports that Lyhan’s petition was considered but received no action.
subfiles.summary: Wilcox tells Lyhan the Senate Education Committee took no action on the Sino-Korean Peoples League petition of March 27 and returned it for filing.

subfiles.title: Native Sons resolution opposing Hawaiʻi statehood
subfiles.from: Grand Parlor, Native Sons of the Golden West
subfiles.about: The resolution urges California’s congressional delegation to oppose Hawaiian statehood on racial, immigration, security, and propaganda grounds.
subfiles.summary: The resolution cites Hawaiʻi’s Asian and Japanese population, possible migration to the mainland, and the pending school-propaganda petition. It demands proof of the territory’s undivided allegiance before statehood should be granted.

subfiles.title: Excerpt from Embassy report on the Society for International Cultural Relations
subfiles.about: The report describes the purposes, leadership, financing, and scholarly activities of Japan’s Society for International Cultural Relations.
subfiles.summary: Embassy report: the Society for International Cultural Relations arose from concern over Japan's image, led by Kabayama and Dan, and is scholarly, liberal, selective and well funded.

subfiles.title: Reference Lists for Teachers, Chapters 1–5
subfiles.about: The pages provide selected readings for teachers covering Japanese geography, history, culture, politics, economics, labor, population, and literature.
subfiles.summary: The lists cite Japanese and Western scholars, literary translations, yearbooks, and studies of modern government and economic conditions. An introductory note directs teachers to a longer bibliography published by the Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai in Tokyo in 1934.

subfiles.title: Navy transmittal of McClatchy letter and propaganda report
subfiles.about: The Navy forwards McClatchy’s letter and a report on Japanese propaganda in American schools to State.
subfiles.summary: Navy letter: a Los Angeles Examiner report says Helen Gay Pratt met Teachers College faculty about Tokyo professors compiling textbooks for American public schools.

subfiles.title: White House memorandum returning McClatchy correspondence
subfiles.about: The White House returns the McClatchy correspondence and asks that it be shown to State.
subfiles.summary: McIntyre relays the President’s suggestion concerning the correspondence. This is another copy of the memorandum appearing earlier in the section.

subfiles.title: Navy memorandum on Japanese propaganda in American schools
subfiles.about: The Navy sends the White House material from the California Joint Immigration Committee concerning Hawaiʻi.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of the June 10 Navy memorandum calling alleged propaganda in American schools pertinent.

subfiles.title: McClatchy letter to Henry L. Roosevelt
subfiles.about: McClatchy presents allegations and enclosures concerning Japanese educational propaganda in Hawaiʻi.
subfiles.summary: He describes the Hawaiian legislative petition, alleged textbook plans, Japanese-language-school material, and reports that the petition was suppressed. He also cites the Senate Education Committee response and Native Sons resolution and offers further information.

subfiles.title: Release 407: Japanese Propaganda in American Public Schools
subfiles.about: This copy alleges a Japanese program to shape American students’ views through textbooks and classroom materials.
subfiles.summary: It quotes claims involving Prince Fushimi, Setsuechi Aoki, Okada, and the Sino-Korean Peoples League protest. The release warns that Japanese-directed materials would impede Americanization in Hawaiʻi.

subfiles.title: Release 408: Japan’s Psychology and American Interests
subfiles.about: This copy presents Japanese imperial ideology and school propaganda as threats to American interests.
subfiles.summary: Release 408: cites Matsuoka, Ichimura, the Pacific fleet and the Nicaragua Canal, then Japanese-prepared textbooks and Hawaii's protest.

subfiles.title: Release 409: High School Students in U.S. to Be Given Books with Correct Information on Japan
subfiles.about: This copy reproduces the Japan Times announcement of a joint Japanese-American textbook project.
subfiles.summary: Release 409: Japanese material to be compiled and reviewed by Lasker and a joint committee as books on modern Japan for American high-school students.

subfiles.title: Release 410: Japan Proposes to Instruct Our Public School Students
subfiles.about: This copy criticizes the proposed Japanese educational program and documents the Hawaiʻi protest.
subfiles.summary: Release 410: ties the Society for International Cultural Relations to government and corporate backing, quotes Okada and Aoki, and alleges textbook plans and defense material for Japanese-language schools.

subfiles.title: Release 420-A: Will Hawaii Suppress Investigation of Japanese Propaganda in Public Schools
subfiles.about: This copy describes Lyhan’s petition, alleged retaliation, and the personnel connected with a Japanese-sponsored textbook.
subfiles.summary: Release 420-A: the Hawaiian Legislature may suppress the investigation, Lyhan was threatened with deportation, and Okada, Lasker, Royama, Pratt and Long figure in the project.

subfiles.title: Hawaiian Senate Education Committee response to Lyhan
subfiles.about: This copy confirms that the Education Committee took no action on the Sino-Korean Peoples League petition.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the Senate Education Committee's response: the petition presented March 27 was returned for filing at session's end.

subfiles.title: Native Sons of the Golden West resolution opposing Hawaiʻi statehood
subfiles.from: Grand Parlor, Native Sons of the Golden West
subfiles.about: This copy urges opposition to Hawaiian statehood pending assurances about security and allegiance.
subfiles.summary: Native Sons of the Golden West resolution citing Hawaii's Asian population and alleged school propaganda, directing California's delegation to oppose statehood until resolved.

subfiles.title: Hull acknowledgment and notice of Interior investigation
subfiles.about: Hull acknowledges the Navy’s submission and reports that Interior has been asked to investigate Japanese propaganda in schools.
subfiles.summary: The letter thanks the Navy for forwarding McClatchy’s correspondence and enclosures. Hull promises further communication after the Interior Department replies.

subfiles.title: Roosevelt transmittal to William Phillips
subfiles.about: Roosevelt sends the State Department correspondence regarding propaganda in Hawaiʻi.
subfiles.summary: The short letter says the enclosed material may interest Phillips’s office. It is another copy of the June 21 transmittal.

subfiles.title: White House memorandum returning McClatchy correspondence
subfiles.about: McIntyre returns the correspondence and conveys the President’s wish that State see it.
subfiles.summary: Further copy of the White House memorandum returning McClatchy correspondence, documenting its presidential referral.

subfiles.title: Navy memorandum on Japanese propaganda in American schools
subfiles.about: The memorandum forwards committee material on propaganda in the Territory of Hawaiʻi.
subfiles.summary: Roosevelt calls the attached information pertinent at the time. This is a further copy of the June 10 Navy memorandum.

subfiles.title: McClatchy letter on Japanese propaganda in Hawaiʻi schools
subfiles.about: This copy forwards allegations, committee releases, and a statehood resolution concerning Japanese activity in Hawaiian schools.
subfiles.summary: McClatchy says the Hawaiian petition was pigeonholed to avoid racial controversy and offers the underlying documentation, with releases and the Native Sons resolution.

subfiles.title: Release 407: Japanese Propaganda in American Public Schools
subfiles.about: This third copy alleges plans for Japanese-produced educational material in American and Hawaiian schools.
subfiles.summary: Release 407: Sino-Korean Peoples League claims that Japanese officials and cultural groups' proposed material would foster Japanism and weaken Americanization.

subfiles.title: Release 408: Japan’s Psychology and American Interests
subfiles.about: This third copy links Japanese expansionism and imperial ideology to propaganda in American schools.
subfiles.summary: Release 408: cites Japanese conduct in the Pacific and the Nicaragua Canal proposal, condemns planned textbooks, and repeats Hawaii's protest.

subfiles.title: Release 409: High School Students in U.S. to Be Given Books with Correct Information on Japan
subfiles.about: This third copy reproduces the Japan Times description of the proposed textbook compilation process.
subfiles.summary: Release 409: a Japanese committee would gather material, Lasker comment, and a joint committee finish books covering modern Japan for American students.

subfiles.title: Release 410: Japan Proposes to Instruct Our Public School Students
subfiles.about: This third copy attacks Japanese-sponsored textbooks and records objections from Hawaiʻi.
subfiles.summary: Release 410: describes government and commercial backing for the Society for International Cultural Relations and warns of defense instruction in Japanese-language schools.

subfiles.title: Release 420-A: Will Hawaii Suppress Investigation of Japanese Propaganda in Public Schools
subfiles.about: This third copy alleges suppression of Lyhan’s investigation request and outlines the preparation of a Japanese-sponsored textbook.
subfiles.summary: Release 420-A: recounts Lyhan's petition, pressure to withdraw it and a threatened deportation, and warns the textbook program would promote Japanization in Hawaii.

subfiles.title: Hawaiian Senate Education Committee response to Lyhan
subfiles.about: This further copy reports the disposition of the Sino-Korean Peoples League petition.
subfiles.summary: Senate Education Committee considered the March 27 petition, took no action, and returned it for filing when the session ended.
